title: Lo que habría dicho
blurbEn: The last text of the unit, and the reason behind a year of Spanish.
body:
Hay una frase que llevo meses queriendo decir en español y todavía no he encontrado el momento.

Es para mi abuela, que cumple ochenta y siete años en julio.

Cuando yo era pequeña, ella me contaba historias todas las noches. Nunca me leyó un libro: se las inventaba sobre la marcha, con personajes que cambiaban de nombre cada noche.

Yo no lo supe hasta los diez años, cuando una prima me lo dijo sin querer. Cuando lo descubrí, me enfadé muchísimo. Le dije que me había mentido durante años. Me sentí traicionada.

Ella se rió y me dijo que las historias inventadas son las únicas que no se acaban nunca, porque nadie las ha escrito.

Habría dado cualquier cosa por entenderlo entonces. Pero hay cosas que solo se entienden tarde.

En julio voy a verla. Para cuando llegue, ya habré preparado la frase.

Ojalá me salga.
translationEn:
There's a sentence I've spent months wanting to say in Spanish and still haven't found the moment for.

It's for my grandmother, who turns eighty-seven in July.

When I was small, she used to tell me stories every night. She never read me a book: she made them up as she went, with characters who changed their names every night.

I didn't find out until I was ten, when a cousin told me without meaning to. When I discovered it, I got furious. I told her she had lied to me for years. I felt betrayed.

She laughed and told me that made-up stories are the only ones that never end, because nobody has written them down.

I would have given anything to understand that then. But there are things you only understand late.

In July I'm going to see her. By the time I arrive, I'll have prepared the sentence.

I hope it comes out right.

había mentido.note: The lying came before the telling-off, which came before now. Three layers of past in one paragraph.

Habría dado.note: A past that never happened — she did not understand, and cannot go back.

habré preparado.note: All three compound tenses appear in this text: había, habría, habré.

phrases.gloss: I hope it comes out right
